title: CTK-02 Node Roles and Capability Capsule Foundation
purpose: Prove that one Locaily installation can identify as a node, assume an implemented role, advertise and evaluate a portable capability capsule, install it by version and hash, attach node-local bindings, and route CTK-01 execution to its eligible host.
problem: CTK-01 proves event-to-capability execution on one local boundary, but it retains the provisional assumption that Local Brain is the installation-wide control component and another machine is merely a capability target. Capability portability and placement require Locaily installations to share one node contract, with Local Brain represented as a role and local configuration kept separate from transferable capability assets.

included: Versioned Locaily node identity contract with installation identity, roles, platform, runtimes, resources, trust, capability inventory, and availability
Implemented brain, worker, and hybrid role declarations with explicit primary_brain configuration
Declared but unimplemented storage, relay, and standby_brain roles
Versioned Capability Capsule package and manifest contract using capability.yaml, workflow.yaml, scripts, schemas, adapters, tests, install, README.md, and checksums.json
Portable, bindable, and anchored portability classifications
Separate node-local binding contract containing references and policy but no raw credentials
File or local-transport advertisement, requirement evaluation, installation, self-test, registration, and binding flow

Explicit durable rejection and provenance for unsupported OS, missing runtime, insufficient resources, missing bindings, disallowed permissions, checksum failure, untrusted source, failed self-test, and incompatible version
Synthetic portable and bindable capability fixtures exercised on multiple local node fixtures
CTK-01 routing to the eligible node that hosts the selected capability
Canonical JSON normalization before hashing, policy evaluation, planning, persistence, or execution
excluded: DBVT SEO Audit integration or DBVT private configuration
LAN discovery, remote execution, relay routing, or automatic brain failover
Transport encryption, production certificate enrollment, or a public capability marketplace
Raw credentials or secrets inside a capability capsule or node binding
Automatic capability-building agents or runtime self-modification

acceptanceCriteria: A Locaily installation identifies itself through the versioned node contract.
The same Locaily software can be configured as Brain, Worker, or Hybrid without separate products.
One node advertises a synthetic versioned capability capsule.
A second node deterministically evaluates the advertised capability requirements.
The second node accepts, installs, self-tests, and registers the capability when all requirements pass.
Each major transfer failure condition is explicitly rejected with a durable reason and provenance record.
A node-local binding can be attached using credential references without storing or exposing raw credentials.
A capability is transferred and identified by version and verified hash rather than an unmanaged folder copy.
One portable capability installs and runs on multiple eligible node fixtures.
One bindable capability installs but remains unavailable until its required local binding is registered.
CTK-01 routes an event to the eligible node hosting the selected capability.
Advertisement, evaluation, installation, binding, routing, execution, and rejection actions have complete provenance.
